blurb: Four Mac minis from 2011, a switch, and a laptop to drive them. One host is provisioned so far; the rest are hardware waiting for an OS.

network.topology: One wired segment: every mini goes to sw-1 over 1000BASE-T, and sessions reach them from air-1 by SSH.
network.disclosure: Addresses, hostnames and key material are deliberately not published here.

stack.name: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS
stack.note: Server install on each mini, replacing the 2011 macOS they shipped with.

stack.name: OpenSSH server
stack.note: The only way onto a mini. Key auth from air-1.

stack.name: Node.js (via nvm)
stack.note: Per-user install, so a mini can be re-pinned without touching the system packages.

stack.name: Claude Code CLI
stack.note: One session per host. That ratio is the whole reason there are four of them.

stack.name: herdr
stack.note: Terminal and session management across the hosts.

stack.name: NFS share for ~/repos
stack.note: Repositories are cloned per host today. A shared mount would save four clones of the same tree.

house_rules: One agent session per host — that ratio is the point of the cluster, not a limitation of it.
Mid-2011 thermals were designed for open air, so the minis sit side by side and are never stacked.
